minutes.headline: Selectmen approved a wine and malt license and appointed one Council on Aging member; land purchase deferred to April 1.
minutes.summary: The board proclaimed Boys and Girls Club week, held two liquor license hearings, and heard an update on a proposed open-space land purchase and agreement. It interviewed committee candidates and appointed one to the Council on Aging. Reports covered transportation funding, the school project site review, and stormwater, followed by a joint workshop with the planning board.

what_happened.line: The Select Board approved a wine and malt license for Kebabalicious after a hearing.
The board approved a change of officer and transfer of stock for Lunenburg Liquors.
The board appointed one candidate to the Council on Aging; a second Council on Aging appointment was tabled pending a check of the bylaw or charter.
The open-space land purchase and sale agreement was deferred to April 1 unless urgency requires a posted meeting.
A personnel committee appointment was deferred until the PAC and Personnel committee reviews, and a report said the state draft capital plan omits funding to finish Summer Street design.

why_it_matters: The open-space purchase would commit town land and money, so the April 1 agreement is where residents may see a proposal that could later reach a Town Meeting vote.

Stormwater structures on public roads fall to the town budget, mostly taxes, which competes with limited road funding, and the missing state design money for Summer Street leaves that project unfunded for now.
watch_next: April 1 Select Board meeting, when the open-space purchase and sale agreement is to be taken up.
The bylaw or charter check that will decide the tabled Council on Aging appointment.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The three votes and the two tabling decisions agree, and the attendee differences are mostly misheard names. The official minutes record many more items, including the warrant, the site plan review decision and several applicants. The main differences to check are the personnel/PACC deferral reason and our unsupported $333 thousand Summer Street figure.
